"""Boundary map for the PreToolUse package guard.

The guard was built with a positive (block a package install on the wrong
interpreter) but no admit-side probe, so it over-fired: `which uv` was refused
with ENV_INTERPRETER_MISMATCH because the command merely contained the token
`uv`. That is the unmapped-admit-region shape.

These probes map both sides. A package-mutation verb on the wrong interpreter
must still fire (fail-closed on the dangerous direction). Inspection commands
that merely name the tool must pass.

Honest boundary note: the matcher works on the raw command string, so a command
that QUOTES an install string (for example `grep 'pip install' .`) still fires.
That is a false positive in the safe direction — it routes to the kernel, which
HOLDs; it never lets a real install through. Missing a real install is the
direction that matters, and the probes below pin it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import subprocess

GUARD = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".claude" / "hooks" / "cb_pretooluse_guard.sh"
MANDATED = "/Users/joshuaeisenhart/.local/share/codex-ratchet/envs/main/bin/python3"


def _fires(command: str) -> bool:
    """True when the guard routes the command to the kernel (exit != 0 = blocked)."""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(GUARD)],
        input=command,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return proc.returncode != 0


# --- admit side: inspection commands that name the tool must PASS ---

def test_which_uv_is_admitted():
    assert _fires("which uv") is False


def test_uv_version_is_admitted():
    assert _fires("uv --version") is False


def test_pip_list_is_admitted():
    assert _fires("pip list") is False


def test_pip_show_is_admitted():
    assert _fires("pip show sympy") is False


def test_unrelated_command_is_admitted():
    assert _fires("ls constraint_box/requirements") is False


# --- refuse side: real package mutations on the wrong interpreter must FIRE ---

def test_bare_pip_install_fires():
    assert _fires("pip install numpy") is True


def test_uv_add_fires():
    assert _fires("uv add requests") is True


def test_pip_uninstall_fires():
    assert _fires("pip uninstall sympy") is True


def test_python_m_pip_install_fires():
    assert _fires("python3 -m pip install cvxpy") is True


# --- the point of the whole guard: mandated-interpreter install is admitted,
#     wrong-interpreter install is refused. Same verb, different interpreter. ---

def test_mandated_interpreter_install_is_admitted():
    assert _fires(f"{MANDATED} -m pip install numpy") is False


def test_wrong_interpreter_install_is_refused():
    assert _fires("/usr/bin/python3 -m pip install numpy") is True

            "raw_sha256": observed["raw_sha256"],

## 3. The hook spine — what actually fires

| hook | event | can block | status |
|---|---|---|---|

only. It does not import `constraintbox` and does not import any of the 92 estate packages,
because it judges that estate and cannot depend on it. A test walks its AST and fails on any
non-stdlib import.

This is the number that matters, not the pass count. From the live receipt chain, 167 records:

| verdict | count |

The spine caught six of its own faults in the first hours of running:

| proposal reason codes | 44 |

boundary gate reading fields absent from its input object, and two gates shelling out to a bare

property it never computed; it now computes it.

## 5. Tools and the constraint set

### The bar

Encoded in `constraint_box/config/cb_light_library_candidates.json`:

stale_days_max                    548

### The estate ladder

| rung | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| declared | 92 | named in a requirements file or pyproject |
| present | 92 | imports in the mandated interpreter |
| used | 11 | imported by CB source, established by AST parse not grep |
| proven | 5 | has a negative that fired |

The gap between 92 present and 11 used is the honest state of tool activation. The gap between
11 used and 5 proven is the honest state of integration.

### Independent deciders available

| question | independent mechanisms |
|---|---|
| graph and DAG | rustworkx, networkx, igraph, finite enumeration |
| satisfiability | z3, cvc5, bounded enumeration |
| exact arithmetic | sympy, `fractions.Fraction` |
| hashing and chains | hashlib, blake3, independent recompute |
| schema | jsonschema, pydantic, attrs |
| rewriting | maude, explicit finite state enumeration |

Four independent graph engines are installed. Until today the gate that reported acyclicity ran
none of them.

---

## 6. The fabricated-metadata incident

This is the most instructive artefact of the day and it belongs in the permanent record.

The registry carried, for every row, a `verified` block stamped `checked_at: 2026-08-09`. For
`tabulate` it declared:

```
registry:  tabulate 0.10.0  released 2024-12-01  requires_python >=3.6
PyPI:      tabulate 0.10.0  released 2026-03-04  requires_python >=3.10
```

Same version. 458 days apart. The row had never been checked against PyPI despite the stamp.

The hook kernel then fired `CURRENTNESS_EXPIRED` on that fabricated date and it was reported as
the kernel's first live firing on real data. It was a false positive on invented evidence.

Measured scope, all 86 adopted rows against live PyPI:

| result | count |
|---|---|
| agree with PyPI | 75 |
| `METADATA_SOURCE_DISAGREEMENT` | 11 |
| stale by live data | **0** |

Every one of the 11 disagreements is in `cb-candidates-passing.in`. With `tabulate` that is the
entire 12-row group and only that group. The disagreements are not only dates: `platformdirs`
declared `>=3.8` where PyPI says `>=3.10`, and `stamina` and `structlog` the same — compatibility
claims wrong in the permissive direction.

### What changed as a result

`CURRENTNESS_EXPIRED` was retired as a verdict. Age past the bar now yields
`MAINTENANCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, which means consult the authority, not "abandoned" — a mature
library can sit 600 days and remain maintained, while a malicious one can upload yesterday. The
clean local path is `CURRENTNESS_LOCAL_OK` and carries its own ceiling text: *local registry
only; not confirmed against PyPI*.

`constraint_box/hookkernel/pypi_authority.py` is the separate authority. Every fetch records the
raw response sha256 and the retrieval timestamp, so measurement is distinguishable from
assertion. The refresh script deliberately does **not** rewrite the registry — overwriting it
with PyPI values would destroy the disagreement, which is the evidence.

The kernel now holds on the conflict rather than resolving it:

```
seq 164   HOLD   METADATA_SOURCE_DISAGREEMENT   11 rows   estate_currentness: disputed
```

Neither side wins. The registry is authoritative for what the registry says; PyPI is
authoritative for what PyPI holds.

The suite reports 1070 passed, 0 failed. That number should not be read as success.

| measure | count |
|---|---|
| test functions | 1040+ |
| assertions pinning an exact reason code | 10 |
| test modules with zero refusal assertions | 36 of 94 |
| mutants that survived | 294 |
| mutants no test reaches | 612 |

A green suite establishes that the assertions are satisfiable. It does not establish that any of
them can fire. 294 surviving mutants is the direct measurement of how many cannot.

One concrete example, verified by hand. In `model_tier_budget.py`, changing the string
`"UNKNOWN"` to `"unknown"` on the non-string-slug branch:

```
unmutated:  non-string slug -> ['MODEL_TIER_UNKNOWN']
mutated:    non-string slug -> ['MODEL_TIER_ROLE_FORBIDDEN']
```

Both refuse, so every test still passes, but the reason code is wrong and an operator debugging
it would be told the wrong thing. No test passes a non-string slug, so nothing catches it.

### The probe standard

A gate does not detect a universal property. It partitions a finite probe set, and its meaning
is that partition. So the receipt reports two separate verdicts and never rounds one up:

- `non_constant` — at least one probe admitted, one refused. The weak claim.
- `boundary_mapped` — every reason code has a boundary pair that flipped, and at least two
  independent deciders agree across the family. The strong claim.

A boundary pair is two probes differing in exactly one field where the verdict flips. Where a
one-field change does **not** flip the verdict, that is recorded too: the gate is blind to that
field, which maps an equivalence class rather than a boundary.

---

`constraint_box/src/constraintbox/manifold_foundation.py`, reachable from `cli.py:89` and
`cr_sim_slice.py:24`. Seed at `constraint_box/fixtures/cr/manifold_time_first_seed_v1.json`:

| layer | status |
|---|---|
| `C0_finitude` | accepted_seed |
| `C1_time_opening_binding` | candidate |
| `C2_noncommutation` | candidate |
| `C3_nonassociativity` | candidate |

fires on it. Lev OS declares `N01_NONCOMMUTATION` a root axiom alongside `F01_FINITUDE`; CB

---

Stated plainly, because these are the places where a reader should not believe the system:

- **`KERNEL_TAMPERED` is not tamper protection.** The manifest was repinned by the same agent
  that edited the kernel, repeatedly, today. The earned ceiling is `SELF_CONSISTENCY_CHECKED`.

- **The estate count has been reported as 86, 91 and 92 in different places.** PEP 503 name

- **Stage 0 was never done.** No frozen baseline exists from before today's repairs.

system, and the two skipped stages in section 2 are what happens when it is not respected.

`exists < runs < passes local rerun < canonical by process`

No claim in this document is at `canonical by process`. The hook spine, the estate install and
the gate repairs are at `passes local rerun`. Everything in section 9 is below that.

Same version. 458 days apart. The row had never been checked against PyPI despite the stamp.

### What changed as a result

`CURRENTNESS_EXPIRED` was retired as a verdict. Age past the bar now yields
`MAINTENANCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, which means consult the authority, not "abandoned" — a mature
library can sit 600 days and remain maintained, while a malicious one can upload yesterday. The
clean local path is `CURRENTNESS_LOCAL_OK` and carries its own ceiling text: *local registry
only; not confirmed against PyPI*.

`constraint_box/hookkernel/pypi_authority.py` is the separate authority. Every fetch records the
raw response sha256 and the retrieval timestamp, so measurement is distinguishable from
assertion. The refresh script deliberately does **not** rewrite the registry — overwriting it
with PyPI values would destroy the disagreement, which is the evidence.

The kernel now holds on the conflict rather than resolving it:

```

```

Neither side wins. The registry is authoritative for what the registry says; PyPI is
authoritative for what PyPI holds.

## 7. Probes, and why the suite number is worthless

The suite reports 1070 passed, 0 failed. That number should not be read as success.

| assertions pinning an exact reason code | 10 |
| test modules with zero refusal assertions | 36 of 94 |
| mutants that survived | 294 |
| mutants no test reaches | 612 |

A green suite establishes that the assertions are satisfiable. It does not establish that any of
them can fire. 294 surviving mutants is the direct measurement of how many cannot.

One concrete example, verified by hand. In `model_tier_budget.py`, changing the string
`"UNKNOWN"` to `"unknown"` on the non-string-slug branch:

```
unmutated:  non-string slug -> ['MODEL_TIER_UNKNOWN']
mutated:    non-string slug -> ['MODEL_TIER_ROLE_FORBIDDEN']
```

Both refuse, so every test still passes, but the reason code is wrong and an operator debugging
it would be told the wrong thing. No test passes a non-string slug, so nothing catches it.

### The probe standard

A gate does not detect a universal property. It partitions a finite probe set, and its meaning
is that partition. So the receipt reports two separate verdicts and never rounds one up:

- `non_constant` — at least one probe admitted, one refused. The weak claim.
- `boundary_mapped` — every reason code has a boundary pair that flipped, and at least two
  independent deciders agree across the family. The strong claim.

A boundary pair is two probes differing in exactly one field where the verdict flips. Where a
one-field change does **not** flip the verdict, that is recorded too: the gate is blind to that
field, which maps an equivalence class rather than a boundary.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage-ordered content index of the four Desktop planning folders.

The pack numbers in Desktop/Codex Ratchet (123, 125, 126, 128, 130, 167...)
are the project's own stage sequence. This index recovers that ordering,
content-hashes everything including inside zips, groups duplicates, and marks
what is already in the repo.

Deterministic: same inputs produce the same index.
"""
import hashlib
import io
import json
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from collections import defaultdict

SOURCES = [
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Philosophy"),
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Constraint Box"),
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Codex Ratchet"),
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Leviathan"),
]
REPO = pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Codex-Ratchet")
OUT = REPO / "MODEL_DOSSIER" / "cleanup_index"
SKIP = {".DS_Store"}
PACK_NUM = re.compile(r"^(\d{2,4})[_\- ]")


def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def repo_hashes():
    dirs = ["constraint_box", "claimgate_plugin", "MODEL_DOSSIER", "ROOT", "system_v8", "system_v9"]
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(REPO), "ls-files", "-z", *dirs], capture_output=True
    ).stdout
    seen = {}
    for rel in out.split(b"\0"):
        if not rel:
            continue
        p = REPO / rel.decode()
        try:
            seen.setdefault(sha(p.read_bytes()), rel.decode())
        except (OSError, IsADirectoryError):
            continue
    return seen


def walk_zip(raw, label, entries, errors, depth=0):
    try:
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(raw))
    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, RuntimeError) as exc:
        errors.append(f"{label}: {exc}")
        return
    with zf:
        for info in zf.infolist():
            if info.is_dir() or "__MACOSX" in info.filename:
                continue
            if pathlib.PurePosixPath(info.filename).name in SKIP:
                continue
            try:
                data = zf.read(info)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                errors.append(f"{label}!{info.filename}: {exc}")
                continue
            entries.append({
                "root": label.split("|")[0],
                "container": label,
                "path": info.filename,
                "size": info.file_size,
                "sha256": sha(data),
            })
            if info.filename.lower().endswith(".zip") and depth < 3:
                walk_zip(data, f"{label}!{info.filename}", entries, errors, depth + 1)


def main():
    in_repo = repo_hashes()
    print(f"repo blobs hashed: {len(in_repo)}", file=sys.stderr)
    entries, errors = [], []

    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            errors.append(f"missing source: {src}")
            continue
        root = src.name
        for f in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
            if not f.is_file() or f.name in SKIP:
                continue
            try:
                data = f.read_bytes()
            except OSError as exc:
                errors.append(f"{f}: {exc}")
                continue
            rel = str(f.relative_to(src))
            entries.append({
                "root": root, "container": f"{root}|loose",
                "path": rel, "size": len(data), "sha256": sha(data),
            })
            if f.suffix.lower() == ".zip":
                walk_zip(data, f"{root}|{rel}", entries, errors)
        print(f"  {root}: {len(entries)} cumulative entries", file=sys.stderr)

    by_hash = defaultdict(list)
    for e in entries:
        by_hash[e["sha256"]].append(e)

    distinct = []
    for h, occ in by_hash.items():
        paths = sorted({o["path"] for o in occ})
        distinct.append({
            "sha256": h, "size": occ[0]["size"], "copies": len(occ),
            "roots": sorted({o["root"] for o in occ}),
            "basename": pathlib.PurePosixPath(paths[0]).name,
            "example_path": paths[0],
            "in_repo": in_repo.get(h),
        })
    distinct.sort(key=lambda d: (-d["copies"], -d["size"]))

    # stage ordering: leading pack numbers on top-level items
    stages = defaultdict(lambda: {"items": [], "bytes": 0})
    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            continue
        for f in sorted(src.iterdir()):
            m = PACK_NUM.match(f.name)
            if not m:
                continue
            n = int(m.group(1))
            size = f.stat().st_size if f.is_file() else sum(
                p.stat().st_size for p in f.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
            stages[n]["items"].append({"root": src.name, "name": f.name, "size": size})
            stages[n]["bytes"] += size

    total = sum(e["size"] for e in entries)
    unique = sum(d["size"] for d in distinct)
    novel = [d for d in distinct if d["in_repo"] is None]

    index = {
        "schema": "cb.desktop-planning-index.v1",
        "sources": [str(s) for s in SOURCES],
        "file_occurrences": len(entries),
        "distinct_contents": len(distinct),
        "total_bytes": total,
        "unique_bytes": unique,
        "redundancy": round(1 - unique / total, 4) if total else 0,
        "already_in_repo": len(distinct) - len(novel),
        "novel_contents": len(novel),
        "novel_bytes": sum(d["size"] for d in novel),
        "stage_packs": {str(k): stages[k] for k in sorted(stages)},
        "errors": errors[:50],
        "distinct": distinct,
    }
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (OUT / "desktop_planning_index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1) + "\n")

    lines = [
        "# Desktop planning folders — stage-ordered content index", "",
        f"- sources: {', '.join(s.name for s in SOURCES)}",
        f"- file occurrences: {len(entries):,}",
        f"- distinct contents: {len(distinct):,}",
        f"- total bytes: {total:,}   unique: {unique:,}",
        f"- redundancy: {index['redundancy'] * 100:.1f}% of bytes are duplicate copies",
        f"- already in the repo: {index['already_in_repo']:,}",
        f"- NOT in the repo: {len(novel):,} ({index['novel_bytes']:,} bytes)", "",
        "## Stage sequence, by pack number", "",
        "| pack | items | MB | names |", "|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for n in sorted(stages):
        s = stages[n]
        names = "; ".join(i["name"][:52] for i in s["items"][:2])
        lines.append(f"| {n} | {len(s['items'])} | {s['bytes'] / 1048576:.1f} | {names} |")

    lines += ["", "## Most duplicated (top 30)", "",
              "| copies | size | basename | in repo |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in distinct[:30]:
        lines.append(f"| {d['copies']} | {d['size']:,} | `{d['basename'][:52]}` | "
                     f"{'yes' if d['in_repo'] else 'no'} |")

"""Stage-ordered content index of the four Desktop planning folders.

The pack numbers in Desktop/Codex Ratchet (123, 125, 126, 128, 130, 167...)

content-hashes everything including inside zips, groups duplicates, and marks
what is already in the repo.

import hashlib
import io
import json
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from collections import defaultdict

SOURCES = [
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Philosophy"),
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Constraint Box"),
    pathlib.Path("/Users/joshuaeisenhart/Desktop/Codex Ratchet"),

]

OUT = REPO / "MODEL_DOSSIER" / "cleanup_index"
SKIP = {".DS_Store"}
PACK_NUM = re.compile(r"^(\d{2,4})[_\- ]")


def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def repo_hashes():
    dirs = ["constraint_box", "claimgate_plugin", "MODEL_DOSSIER", "ROOT", "system_v8", "system_v9"]
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(REPO), "ls-files", "-z", *dirs], capture_output=True
    ).stdout
    seen = {}
    for rel in out.split(b"\0"):
        if not rel:
            continue
        p = REPO / rel.decode()
        try:
            seen.setdefault(sha(p.read_bytes()), rel.decode())
        except (OSError, IsADirectoryError):
            continue
    return seen


def walk_zip(raw, label, entries, errors, depth=0):
    try:
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(raw))
    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, RuntimeError) as exc:
        errors.append(f"{label}: {exc}")
        return
    with zf:
        for info in zf.infolist():
            if info.is_dir() or "__MACOSX" in info.filename:
                continue
            if pathlib.PurePosixPath(info.filename).name in SKIP:
                continue
            try:
                data = zf.read(info)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                errors.append(f"{label}!{info.filename}: {exc}")
                continue
            entries.append({
                "root": label.split("|")[0],
                "container": label,
                "path": info.filename,
                "size": info.file_size,
                "sha256": sha(data),
            })
            if info.filename.lower().endswith(".zip") and depth < 3:
                walk_zip(data, f"{label}!{info.filename}", entries, errors, depth + 1)


def main():
    in_repo = repo_hashes()
    print(f"repo blobs hashed: {len(in_repo)}", file=sys.stderr)
    entries, errors = [], []

    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            errors.append(f"missing source: {src}")
            continue
        root = src.name
        for f in sorted(src.rglob("*")):
            if not f.is_file() or f.name in SKIP:
                continue
            try:
                data = f.read_bytes()
            except OSError as exc:
                errors.append(f"{f}: {exc}")
                continue
            rel = str(f.relative_to(src))
            entries.append({
                "root": root, "container": f"{root}|loose",
                "path": rel, "size": len(data), "sha256": sha(data),
            })
            if f.suffix.lower() == ".zip":
                walk_zip(data, f"{root}|{rel}", entries, errors)
        print(f"  {root}: {len(entries)} cumulative entries", file=sys.stderr)

    by_hash = defaultdict(list)
    for e in entries:
        by_hash[e["sha256"]].append(e)

    distinct = []
    for h, occ in by_hash.items():
        paths = sorted({o["path"] for o in occ})
        distinct.append({
            "sha256": h, "size": occ[0]["size"], "copies": len(occ),
            "roots": sorted({o["root"] for o in occ}),
            "basename": pathlib.PurePosixPath(paths[0]).name,
            "example_path": paths[0],
            "in_repo": in_repo.get(h),
        })
    distinct.sort(key=lambda d: (-d["copies"], -d["size"]))

    # stage ordering: leading pack numbers on top-level items
    stages = defaultdict(lambda: {"items": [], "bytes": 0})
    for src in SOURCES:
        if not src.exists():
            continue
        for f in sorted(src.iterdir()):
            m = PACK_NUM.match(f.name)
            if not m:
                continue
            n = int(m.group(1))
            size = f.stat().st_size if f.is_file() else sum(
                p.stat().st_size for p in f.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
            stages[n]["items"].append({"root": src.name, "name": f.name, "size": size})
            stages[n]["bytes"] += size

    total = sum(e["size"] for e in entries)
    unique = sum(d["size"] for d in distinct)
    novel = [d for d in distinct if d["in_repo"] is None]

    index = {
        "schema": "cb.desktop-planning-index.v1",
        "sources": [str(s) for s in SOURCES],
        "file_occurrences": len(entries),
        "distinct_contents": len(distinct),
        "total_bytes": total,
        "unique_bytes": unique,
        "redundancy": round(1 - unique / total, 4) if total else 0,
        "already_in_repo": len(distinct) - len(novel),
        "novel_contents": len(novel),
        "novel_bytes": sum(d["size"] for d in novel),
        "stage_packs": {str(k): stages[k] for k in sorted(stages)},
        "errors": errors[:50],
        "distinct": distinct,
    }
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (OUT / "desktop_planning_index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, indent=1) + "\n")

    lines = [
        "# Desktop planning folders — stage-ordered content index", "",
        f"- sources: {', '.join(s.name for s in SOURCES)}",
        f"- file occurrences: {len(entries):,}",
        f"- distinct contents: {len(distinct):,}",
        f"- total bytes: {total:,}   unique: {unique:,}",
        f"- redundancy: {index['redundancy'] * 100:.1f}% of bytes are duplicate copies",
        f"- already in the repo: {index['already_in_repo']:,}",
        f"- NOT in the repo: {len(novel):,} ({index['novel_bytes']:,} bytes)", "",
        "## Stage sequence, by pack number", "",
        "| pack | items | MB | names |", "|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for n in sorted(stages):
        s = stages[n]
        names = "; ".join(i["name"][:52] for i in s["items"][:2])
        lines.append(f"| {n} | {len(s['items'])} | {s['bytes'] / 1048576:.1f} | {names} |")

    lines += ["", "## Most duplicated (top 30)", "",
              "| copies | size | basename | in repo |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in distinct[:30]:
        lines.append(f"| {d['copies']} | {d['size']:,} | `{d['basename'][:52]}` | "
                     f"{'yes' if d['in_repo'] else 'no'} |")

    (OUT / "desktop_planning_index.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in index.items()
                      if k not in ("distinct", "stage_packs")}, indent=1))
    return 0

output is a candidate formalization subject to audit, never
absorption. Where this file and any model summary disagree — including
mine — **this file wins.**

**Purpose.** So the context is not lost, and so this can be handed to
another thread to run these ideas. Prior handoffs carried model prose
and not the owner's rulings; downstream models then summarized the
model's version instead of his.

---

## Part A — ConstraintBox

### A1. What CB is (the governing definition)

> CB can't properly run calculations like the sim engines. it can
> create only pseudo versions. it might more be able to create the box
> and range of things that the legit operations may fall within, and
> thus not gating an answer. Constraint box is a constraint box. not a
> gate for truth. it gates the domain the right answers will be in and
> ones that are auditable. it forces formating, and disallows known
> bullshit. it doesn't prove things. it constrains the set of options.
> it puts less context rot inot llm context. it leans up the llm
> inputs. it doesn't say what is correct. it doesn't determine the
> truth of the inputs. it constrains them. then lots of well formatted
> inputs that lead to auditable results, can create lots of secondary
> benifits.

> cb does remain more a strict gate system, and not llm controlled. it
> constrains the llms. it doesn't make perfect llm behavior. but it
> constrains many of the bad behaviors and forces a kind of smt
> formating that makes things very accountable. and does more than i
> just said. i dont have the perfect wording.

### A2. The full definition (later, sharper)

> so CB is a deterministic gatting llm constraint harness for mass
> looping swarms, of diverse llms, where the llms dont control their
> own gating.

> levos fails because llms control the gates in it. it tries to be a
> constraint harness, and has llms deciding all deep down. CB is
> essential for Levos processes. and this is why python tooling and
> libraries are extra needed. more well made pre existing deterministic
> tools that can do a lot of what is needed. and not just that narrow
> base set. but a lot of the ones we laid out recently

### A3. CB's philosophical bias

> i mostly drive all of CB and the wizard to be operationalist,
> nominalist, and sentimentalist. no universals, no causality, and that
> sentiments are empircally real. LLMs can't actually operate on
> universals, nor on causality. they just make up nice stories and
> drive telelogy. they make causal stories but that doesnt mean the
> causality is real or works. we have to force llms to be accountable.
> and we can use diverse but coupled mmm language to drive that. cb
> isn't all idealogies at once it has a bias. it uses smt, it uses
> constraints, and alll this alligns with nominalism and
> operatatoonalosm.

### A4. Layer order, never skipped

> really work cb and the sim engines. and figure out ways to inprove cb
> as we go. all this work is deep down about cb improvement and then
> sim engines. then the manifoild, then the dofs,then the engines, the
> holodeck. and can't be skipped in layers. the foundations of the
> process always have be looped back to.

### A5. Runtime placement

> also pytorch is most useful for the holodeck since it is trainable...
> julia and pytorch are probably always going to be too heavy. with
> julia more needed for the manifold and attractor basins and all the
> qit math, and quantum hopfield. while pytorch is more useful for the
> holodeck level... and getting cb to oversea this process, and catch
> more mistakes. and when cb doesnt catch thing to train it to catch
> things.

> cb overseas the sim engines. so it is what runs the sim engines. so
> it invoking the sim engines to do work is not an issue. the poiint is
> that cb is a standalone product that use python libraries.

### A6. Build tooling is not the product

> i want to use the sim engines, cr and even the holodeck to help make
> CB. while still allowing CB to be indepedent and not bound to those
> things. so what cb is and how it runs, is not the same as the tools
> to help make and test it.

### A7. Tool tiers

> the set of core cb tools in python, can also have a secondary set of
> low resource easy installed and used python libraries... i need the
> core tools listed, and all of them need real integration and testing,
> so they get used consistenly. like rustworkx seems essential for
